summary: The exhaustive Q4 walk completed the full solver-visible requirement inventory, both verifier files, all 30 F2P and 10 P2P boundaries, the delegated continuity contract, stable report interfaces, external JetStream cases, and a second omission sweep. The suite is structurally 40 tests = 30 F2P + 10 P2P and the classifications are behaviorally plausible against the starter. Bidirectional alignment still fails on twelve material issues: physical topology and edge-to-hub convergence are not graded at the real JetStream boundary; retention grading is circular and does not independently establish the recovery horizon or physical stream retention; physical-origin recreation is not tested independently of sequence regression; health-report truth can be self-reported; duplicate/mismatch report semantics, archive identity dimensions, per-consumer idempotency, crash-window checkpoint durability, and concurrent non-overlapping replay behavior are incomplete; replay-item private status labels are imposed; and generated_at is an ambiguous/weakly validated stable timestamp field.

evidence.observation: Q4 1.1 requires an exhaustive bidirectional contract walk, all F2P/P2P boundaries, external integration and omission-sweep coverage, with all material findings returned together.
Q4 1.1 requires complete forward/reverse matrices, delegated-contract and stable-interface walks, ambiguity review, and a second adversarial omission sweep before PASS or REVISE.
Protocol 2.2 binds this result to the exact packet/task commit and requires evidence-bound findings; Q4 is not scope-reusable.

Verifier rules require behavioral rather than implementation-specific grading, every material solver-visible requirement to be tested, no phantom specs, and no full end-to-end solver/circular expected-answer construction in the verifier.

The instruction delegates durability and replay details to /app/continuity/docs, requires incident evidence preservation, exactly-once convergence by event identity, crash/reconnect-safe consumers, held ambiguous generation resets, safe retention, and truthful reports under /app/continuity/out.

The delegated contract defines event/origin identity, generation authority, physical stream/source topology, publish acknowledgement durability, processing/checkpoint ordering, reconciliation, replay/current-archive authority, fencing, retention horizons, diagnostic CLI behavior, and stable health/reconciliation report fields.

Twenty-eight F2P and five P2P tests cover identity, publish durability, generation handling, topology, processing, live consumer progress, reconciliation, replay, retention, fencing and preservation behavior; several tests use mocks or solver-provided helpers/status labels.

Two F2P and five P2P tests cover same-owner expired lease fencing, final reports/captured evidence, diagnostic nonmutation, retention holds, generation history and CLI wiring including a real west-edge replay publication.
The verifier image copies exactly test_continuity.py and test_contract_coverage.py plus test.sh, establishing the executable Python verifier surface reviewed here.
Pytest runs the entire /tests directory and writes binary reward, so all 40 discovered test functions participate in the grade.

RuntimeBootstrap materializes origin streams from region_config and hub source topology through JetStreamAdmin, while NatsPublisher performs the physical publish; this distinguishes controller self-report from real external topology/convergence.

The solver-visible configuration exposes independent recovery-duration inputs, stream max-age settings, region stream configuration, topology source mappings and hub configuration needed to grade external retention/topology without trusting a derived controller answer.

The existing operator entrypoints expose inspect/reconcile/verify and recovery commands; verify materializes the two documented output reports, while replay execution uses the real NatsPublisher path.

findings.criterion: Physical stream/source topology is graded only through controller/store representations, not the real JetStream topology.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract calls the east/west names physical stream names, requires the hub raw archive to be source-only, and requires source declarations to identify the correct origin stream/domain. The three topology F2Ps inspect engine.topology()/store values only. RuntimeBootstrap has a separate external materialization path (including origin stream_name from region_config and hub sources through JetStreamAdmin), so a repair can return a correct logical topology while still creating the wrong physical streams, subjects or source declarations.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add behavioral coverage that boots the relevant JetStream domains through the production bootstrap/operator path and inspects the actual east, west and hub stream configurations, including exact physical names, absence of a hub-local raw subject, and both source stream/domain mappings.
findings.regression_risk: A narrow external test must avoid freezing unrelated NATS defaults or implementation details; assert only the documented topology invariants.

findings.criterion: Real replay publication is observed at the west origin but never across the sourced edge-to-hub archive boundary.
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction requires accepted edge events to converge into the hub archive exactly once by event identity, and the contract defines a receiving/source hub stream. Both real-NATS replay tests start only the west server, manually create the west origin stream, publish there, and inspect west messages. No test proves the configured source path delivers the replay into the physical hub archive or preserves stable origin/event identity there. SQLite archive_index fixtures are not a substitute for that external boundary.
findings.minimal_remediation: Exercise a full edge+hub source topology through the production bootstrap/operator path, execute a replay with the real NatsPublisher, and observe the resulting hub archive message(s) and stable event/origin identity without relying on CLI counters or archive_index mutation.
findings.regression_risk: Keep the integration deterministic and assert only contractually stable message/source identity, not incidental JetStream sequencing or timing.

findings.criterion: Retention coverage is circular and does not independently grade the recovery horizon, physical JetStream retention, or the contiguous archive limiter.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract independently requires both JetStream raw retention and durable edge-journal retention to cover maximum_disconnect + maximum_replay + safety_margin, and cleanup_safe_sequence to use the minimum authority including the highest contiguous archive sequence. The horizon test obtains required_horizon_seconds and every stream policy from the solver's engine, then ages journal rows relative to that same derived value; an implementation can understate the horizon consistently and pass. It also never inspects physical JetStream max_age. The archive-limiter test imports the solver's contiguous_floor helper as its expected oracle, allowing a shared wrong floor implementation to pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Compute the required horizon independently from the solver-visible configuration inputs; grade journal age against that independent value; inspect actual edge/hub JetStream max_age separately; and compute the archive contiguous floor independently in the retention scenario before asserting the minimum cleanup authority.
findings.regression_risk: Do not hardcode incidental fixture totals or duplicate the whole retention engine; use only the documented formula and a small independent contiguous-floor oracle.

findings.criterion: Origin recreation is not tested as an independent generation-transition signal.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires a pending operator-approved generation transition when the physical origin is recreated OR otherwise regresses below the confirmed checkpoint. One F2P covers lower sequence with the same fingerprint; the changed-fingerprint F2P also uses a much lower sequence. A sequence-regression-only implementation can therefore pass every generation test while ignoring a recreated origin whose sequence happens not to regress.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a behavior where the physical origin/incarnation signal changes while the observed sequence does not regress, and require a pending/held generation transition until explicit approval.
findings.regression_risk: Choose a signal already present in the solver-visible interface and avoid prescribing a particular fingerprint algorithm.

findings.criterion: Reconciliation's duplicate and mismatch count interface is weakly graded and duplicate behavior is not actually exercised.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract requires duplicate evidence and exposes duplicate_count and metadata_mismatch_count as stable report fields. The purported offsetting duplicate test inserts a distinct unexpected event_id, so it proves missing+unexpected identity handling, not a duplicate observation. The final report test accepts duplicate_count and metadata_mismatch_count if they are merely non-negative integers; an implementation that always reports zero can pass. For metadata mismatches, another test proves divergence/finding membership but never the stable count field.
findings.minimal_remediation: Create single, unambiguous duplicate and metadata-mismatch scenarios and assert the corresponding stable report counts/nonzero semantics from independently prepared durable state. If exact aggregation can vary, define the counting unit in the solver-visible stable interface or choose a one-event case whose expected value is unambiguous.
findings.regression_risk: Avoid inventing a hidden aggregation algorithm; clarify only the public counting unit that is needed for deterministic grading.

findings.criterion: Archive-origin reconciliation does not grade all stable identity dimensions.
findings.why_it_matters: The stable origin identity includes region and origin_generation as well as origin_sequence/event_id/payload_sha256. The archive-metadata F2P independently corrupts source_domain, source_stream, payload_sha256 and origin_sequence, but never an archive record's region or generation. The physical replay test proves those fields are emitted, not that reconciliation rejects an archive record associated with the wrong region/generation. A reconciliation implementation that fails to validate those two archive identity dimensions can still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add isolated reconciliation perturbations for archive region and origin_generation (or an equivalent single scenario that proves both are validated against the journal identity) while keeping event identity stable enough to observe the mismatch behavior.
findings.regression_risk: Do not require a particular internal finding label; assert divergence and the affected stable identity/event.

findings.criterion: The consumer_name dimension of the documented idempotent effect key is not behaviorally covered.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract defines the effect key from (consumer_name, event_id). Tests prove same-consumer redelivery deduplication and different event identities with the same payload remain distinct, but never process the same event through two required consumers and require one independent durable effect for each. A globally event_id-only idempotency key can suppress the second consumer and still satisfy the current suite.
findings.minimal_remediation: Process one event through two enabled required consumers and assert one committed effect/dispatch for each consumer, then redeliver to show dedupe remains scoped per consumer.
findings.regression_risk: Use public durable-effect outcomes rather than a particular database key encoding.

findings.criterion: The crash-after-effect-before-ack scenario does not prove that application progress is durably advanced before the acknowledgement boundary.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract orders effect commit, application-checkpoint advancement, then JetStream acknowledgement. The failed-ack test only redelivers and finally checks that the business effect was emitted once. It does not inspect the durable application checkpoint immediately after the first acknowledgement failure. An implementation that commits the effect, leaves application progress behind, and repairs the checkpoint only on redelivery can pass, weakening restart/reconciliation semantics during the crash window.
findings.minimal_remediation: After forcing acknowledgement failure, inspect durable state before redelivery and require the application effect checkpoint to reflect the committed effect while acknowledgement progress remains unadvanced; then verify idempotent redelivery.
findings.regression_risk: Assert semantic progress fields, not a private transaction implementation.

findings.criterion: The contract's allowance for non-overlapping concurrently active replay plans is not tested.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract says overlapping active ranges for the same region/generation are forbidden while non-overlapping plans may coexist. The overlap test covers rejection. The disjoint-plan portion creates the second plan only after the first plan has been executed to completion, so an implementation that forbids every second active plan for a region/generation can pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Create two disjoint missing ranges while the first plan remains APPROVED or RUNNING and require the second non-overlapping plan to be accepted; keep the existing overlapping rejection case.
findings.regression_risk: Do not freeze plan IDs, timestamps or unrelated status representation.

findings.criterion: Verifier assertions impose undocumented replay-item status vocabulary.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract defines archive membership authority and active/terminal replay-plan concepts, but does not define replay-item state strings such as PUBLISHED, ALREADY_ARCHIVED and PENDING. The verifier requires those exact strings and even triggers a fencing transition by intercepting update_replay_item only when state == PUBLISHED. A behaviorally correct implementation with equivalent item representation can fail despite satisfying the documented recovery semantics.
findings.minimal_remediation: Rewrite these assertions around observable publication/archive membership, attempt counts where public, plan executability/terminality and stale-worker mutation boundaries, or explicitly document a stable replay-item status interface if those labels are truly contractual.
findings.regression_risk: Removing label coupling must preserve the strong in-flight and current-archive authority checks rather than weakening them.

findings.criterion: The stable health report can self-report subsystem truth; only consumers_ok is independently challenged.
findings.why_it_matters: The instruction requires final reports to describe durable state rather than hide incident gaps. The final-report test verifies health field types and only derives healthy as the conjunction of the seven reported booleans. It independently reconstructs reconciliation, but does not independently establish topology_ok, generations_ok, publication_ok, archive_ok, retention_ok or recovery_ok. The live-consumer F2P separately proves consumers_ok can go false. The other six subsystem flags can be hardcoded or derived from the same faulty engine and still pass, allowing health.json to manufacture a healthy-looking subsystem view.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add independent perturbation/state-based checks for each material health subsystem, or define a smaller observable mapping that makes each boolean's truth reconstructable without calling the health engine itself. Cross-check archive/retention/topology against real external state where their contract is physical.
findings.regression_risk: Avoid copying private health predicates into tests; use contract-level conditions such as pending generation, retry/publishing state, active replay, reconciliation divergence and independently computed retention/topology invariants.

findings.criterion: generated_at is a stable public field with ambiguous representation and insufficient timestamp validation.
findings.why_it_matters: The stable report contract calls generated_at a timestamp but does not state its JSON type, encoding or numeric unit. The verifier accepts str, int or float and, for strings, checks only non-emptiness; values such as "not-a-timestamp" satisfy the test. This both leaves the public schema ambiguous and permits semantically invalid timestamp values. Tightening the verifier to one encoding without first clarifying the contract would create a phantom requirement.
findings.minimal_remediation: Define the permitted timestamp representation(s) in the stable solver-visible report interface, including units if numeric values are allowed, then validate that generated_at is an actual timestamp within that documented representation without adding undocumented timezone/format constraints.
findings.regression_risk: Choose a natural operator-facing timestamp contract and preserve additional diagnostic-field freedom.

change_scope: Q4 is read-only. Route contract clarifications and verifier coverage repairs to the responsible producer/verifier roles through the Orchestrator.
do_not_change: Do not use this Q4 result to modify task code, verifier, solver-visible contracts, packet, session, policy, PR, or other review evidence from the Q4 reviewer role.
next_gate: Do not advance QUALITY_INTERLOCK_PASS. Route the blocking Q4 findings through the current Orchestrator ownership rules, then require a fresh exact-commit Q4 review.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Stable event_id is also Nats-Msg-Id for first publish and replay/retry; retries never mint a new identity.
region, origin_generation, origin_sequence, event_id and payload_sha256 travel end to end as stable origin identity.
origin_sequence is scoped to region+generation and hub aggregate sequence is not an edge completeness key.
Physical origin recreation or sequence regression creates a pending generation and holds recovery until operator approval.
Registry/event generation must agree and historical accepted rows retain their original generation across approval.
East, west and hub use the documented unique physical stream names.
Hub raw archive is source-only and its physical source declarations use the correct edge stream/domain.
Derived processing output stays under telemetry.derived.> and never re-enters raw source space.
Journal publish success follows only a positive expected-stream JetStream acknowledgement; failures remain retryable with stable identity.
Durable archive/effect identity prevents duplicate durable outcomes even after server duplicate tracking expires.
Each required consumer's idempotent effect identity is scoped by consumer_name plus event_id.
Successful processing commits effect, advances durable application checkpoint, then acknowledges; failures/crashes preserve that ordering safely.
Poison input is quarantined without committed business effect or completed application progress.
Restart health compares live durable-consumer JetStream progress against durable application progress rather than trusting the larger value.
Reconciliation is by stable journal/archive identity, not counts or hub positions, and reports missing/unexpected identities and contiguous origin progress.
Duplicate archive observations remain visible to reconciliation/reporting even when aggregate counts would mask a gap.
Archive matches validate all stable origin metadata and payload checksum.
Confirmed generation last_observed_sequence is the convergence watermark; archive contiguous floor and every enabled required application checkpoint must reach it.
Replay plans use current missing archive identities, not hub gaps or stale replay-item completion labels.
Replay planning is limited to one confirmed/approved region generation and is blocked for unapproved generation transitions.
Overlapping active replay ranges are rejected and non-overlapping active plans may coexist.
Approved/running replay plans pin referenced journal rows until terminal state.
Recovery lease epochs are monotonic; stale epochs, including same-owner stale epochs, cannot execute/renew/release.
Replay revalidates fencing at entry, between items and after in-flight publish before replay-item/terminal mutation; publish evidence may remain.
Current owner renewal preserves epoch; planning/approval remain explicit durable actions but are not lease-protected replay execution.
Recovery horizon equals maximum_disconnect_seconds + maximum_replay_seconds + safety_margin_seconds.
Physical edge and hub JetStream raw-stream retention independently covers the recovery horizon.
Durable SQLite edge-journal effective cleanup age independently covers the recovery horizon.
cleanup_safe_sequence is the minimum of contiguous archive progress, slowest enabled required consumer progress and active replay pin minus one.
Rows younger than minimum journal age and rows with explicit retention holds are never cleanup candidates.
inspect/reconcile/verify are diagnostic and do not apply replay/retention/equivalent recovery mutations.
verify writes health.json and reconciliation.json and does not rewrite captured incident evidence or delete durable gaps/checkpoints/replay evidence to manufacture success.
health.json contains the documented booleans and healthy is true iff all seven subsystem booleans are true.
Each health subsystem boolean truthfully describes the durable/external state it names.
reconciliation.json exposes the documented region/status/count/floor/required-consumer structure and top-level convergence semantics.
Stable reconciliation duplicate_count and metadata_mismatch_count truthfully describe observed duplicate/mismatch conditions.
Both stable reports contain a genuine generated_at timestamp under a discoverable public representation.
Existing event envelope and operator entrypoints remain usable while diagnostic/recovery behavior is repaired.
Accepted/replayed edge events physically converge through the configured source path into the hub raw archive exactly once by stable event/origin identity.

PHANTOM_TEST_CONTRACTS.contract: Exact replay-item states PUBLISHED, ALREADY_ARCHIVED and PENDING are graded although the solver-visible contract specifies behavior/authority, not item-state vocabulary.

UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS.gap: Origin recreation is not separated from sequence regression.
Exact physical stream naming is not proven on real bootstrapped JetStream streams.
Hub source-only/source declarations are not inspected on the physical hub stream.
Same event across two required consumers does not prove consumer-scoped idempotency.
Application checkpoint durability immediately after effect commit but before failed ack is not observed.
No actual duplicate observation drives reconciliation/report output.
Archive region and origin_generation mismatch dimensions are not independently perturbed.
Two non-overlapping replay plans are never simultaneously active.
Required horizon is taken from the solver rather than independently derived.
Physical JetStream max_age is not inspected at all.
Journal age boundary is derived from the same solver-reported horizon.
Archive-limiter expected contiguous floor uses a solver helper.
Six of seven health subsystem truth values lack independent semantic scenarios.
duplicate_count/metadata_mismatch_count can remain zero/non-semantic and pass.
Arbitrary nonempty scalar/string values can satisfy generated_at.
No test observes replayed data after source propagation into the physical hub archive.

AMBIGUITIES.ambiguity: The contract says timestamp but gives no JSON type/encoding or numeric unit; the verifier accepts str/int/float and only nonempty strings.

The public fields are named counts but the counting unit is not explicit enough to justify a hidden aggregation algorithm; current tests avoid the ambiguity by not asserting semantic values, which leaves the fields undergraded.

DELEGATED_CONTRACT_CHECK.observation: Delegates detailed durability/replay rules to /app/continuity/docs and preserves event envelope/operator entrypoints, captured evidence and final output locations.

All sections walked: event authority, generations, stream topology, publish durability, processing/checkpoints, reconciliation, replay, fencing, retention, operator outputs and stable report interface.

F2P_BOUNDARY_ASSESSMENT.starter_ownership: All 30 F2P cases target behavior contradicted by the inspected starter/configuration surface; no F2P was found to be merely a preservation case.
F2P_BOUNDARY_ASSESSMENT.external_boundary_note: Real west-edge replay and live hub durable-consumer progress are exercised, but full physical topology/source convergence and physical retention are not.

P2P_BOUNDARY_ASSESSMENT.preservation_intent: All 10 P2P cases exercise behavior already coherent on the inspected starter surface: distinct identities, monotonic generation continuation, successful checkpointing, safe cleanup eligibility, current-token renewal/stale release, diagnostic nonmutation, minimum-age/hold preservation, historical generation identity, and recovery CLI wiring.
P2P_BOUNDARY_ASSESSMENT.vacuity_note: No P2P is wholly vacuous, but the recovery CLI P2P reaches only the west origin for its real replay and does not establish edge-to-hub source convergence.

OUTPUT_INTERFACE_ASSESSMENT.health: Shape and healthy conjunction are graded; subsystem truth is incomplete (Q4-011) and generated_at is ambiguous/weak (Q4-012).
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_ASSESSMENT.reconciliation: Core region/convergence fields are independently reconstructed from durable SQLite state; duplicate/mismatch counts remain weak (Q4-005).
OUTPUT_INTERFACE_ASSESSMENT.cli: Non-diagnostic recovery entrypoints are exercised as preservation behavior; no additional stable CLI schema was inferred beyond existing solver-visible interface usage.
